title: Korean Hotteok with Brown Sugar and Walnuts
summary: Sweet Korean-style yeasted pancakes with a sticky brown sugar, cinnamon and walnut filling. They are crisp and golden outside, chewy inside, and best served hot as a dessert or street-food treat.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil, plus extra for shaping and frying

steps: Mix the plain flour, dried yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the lukewarm milk and 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil, then stir to make a soft, sticky dough.
Cover the bowl and leave the dough in a warm place for 45 minutes, until puffed and roughly doubled in size.
Meanwhile, mix the brown sugar, chopped walnuts and cinnamon in a small bowl for the filling.
Lightly oil your hands and a work surface. Divide the risen dough into 8 equal pieces and flatten each piece into a small disc.
Put a spoonful of the walnut sugar filling in the centre of each disc. Pinch the edges tightly together to seal, then gently shape into a ball with the seam underneath.
Heat the remaining vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the filled dough balls seam-side down, leaving space between them, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden.

Flip the pancakes and press each one gently with a spatula to flatten. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then flip once more and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes until both sides are deep golden and crisp and the filling has melted.
Let the hotteok cool for 2 minutes before eating, as the sugar filling will be very hot.
